paragraphs: Villagers in central India are protesting against a massive government project to link two major rivers in order to help millions of local farmers.

The plan aims to build a large dam and move water to areas facing severe drought; however, construction work has already caused rising waters to flood nearby villages, homes, and a local temple. Angry residents say the government is not giving them enough money or a new place to rebuild their lives. Some protesters have even taken extreme actions, like lying on fake funeral fires to show their anger.

At the same time, environmental experts warn that the new dam will destroy large areas of forest and harm rare wildlife inside a famous tiger reserve. While government officials claim the project will solve long-term water shortages and bring power to the region, critics argue the scientific plans are flawed and urge leaders to protect both local communities and nature.

paragraphs: In India, many villagers are protesting against a big government plan to join two rivers.

The government wants to build a big dam to bring water to dry areas and help farmers grow food. But rising water from the construction is already flooding homes, farmland, and temples. Local people say the government is taking their land without giving them enough money or a new home. Some protesters say they will not leave their land. Nature experts are also worried because the project will flood a large forest and hurt tigers living in a famous reserve.
Government leaders say the project is needed to solve water problems, but many locals and experts want the government to stop and fix these serious problems first.
